patient_information: A 34-year-old man from northern Peru, living in Chile for 9 years. He is cachectic with a BMI of 17. His mother and one brother died from chronic abdominal symptoms and wasting of unknown origin. His Peruvian wife and children were reported as healthy initially.
chief_complaint: A 6-month history of severe chronic diarrhoea with colicky abdominal pain and a 20 kg weight loss.
history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a 6-month history of severe chronic diarrhoea, colicky abdominal pain, and a weight loss of approximately 20 kg. For more than 12 years, he has suffered from recurrent episodes of diarrhoea and abdominal cramps, with an increased frequency over the past 2 years.
exposure_and_epidemiology: The patient originates from northern Peru, a tropical region endemic for Strongyloides stercoralis and HTLV-1. He has resided in Chile for the past 9 years. His family history is notable for a mother and brother who died from similar chronic wasting illnesses. Subsequent testing revealed asymptomatic S. stercoralis infection in his wife and one child, and his wife also tested positive for HTLV-1.
vitals: The patient was afebrile on presentation.
physical_exam: The patient was cachectic with severe loss of muscle mass, weighing 44 kg (BMI 17). Physical examination revealed slight pain on abdominal palpation but was otherwise normal, with no enlargement of the liver or spleen, no palpable lymphadenopathy, and no peripheral oedema.
labs_and_diagnostics: Laboratory results showed a WBC of 11.7 x 10^9/L, hemoglobin of 12.4 g/dL, total protein of 4.9 g/dL, and albumin of 2.2 g/dL. An HIV test was negative. Abdominal CT and MRI scans were without pathological findings. An oesophagogastroduodenoscopy was macroscopically normal, but a duodenal biopsy showed chronic duodenitis with structures compatible with a helminth infection. A Baermann test on a stool sample demonstrated a high load of rhabditiform larvae of S. stercoralis. Larvae were also found in respiratory secretions but not in urine. HTLV-1 serology was confirmed to be positive.
differential_diagnosis: The differential diagnosis for chronic diarrhoea and wasting included helminth infections, specifically Strongyloides stercoralis and Capillaria philippinensis, which are known to cause such severe symptoms. Given the patient's origin from a region endemic for S. stercoralis, this was considered the most probable cause. Intestinal protozoa like Cryptosporidium or Cystoisospora belli were also considered, particularly in the context of a potential immunocompromised state.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient was hospitalized and stabilized with symptomatic treatment and parenteral nutrition. He was treated with oral ivermectin (200 µg/kg per day) for 7 days, which was repeated after 2 weeks. He recovered from his diarrhoea and abdominal symptoms within weeks. A parasitological follow-up examination at 3 months was negative, and he had gained 13 kg. His wife and one child were also treated for asymptomatic S. stercoralis infection.
final_diagnosis: The final diagnosis was Strongyloides stercoralis hyperinfection syndrome associated with HTLV-1 coinfection. The diagnosis was established by the clinical presentation of severe chronic diarrhea and wasting, confirmed by the identification of a high load of S. stercoralis rhabditiform larvae in both stool (via Baermann testing) and respiratory secretions. The underlying predisposing immunodeficiency was identified as HTLV-1 infection, confirmed by serology. The patient's dramatic clinical and weight improvement after ivermectin treatment further supported the diagnosis.
